text:
arjun: FYI we're seeing a spike in fn_call schema rejects coinciding with quota routing changes this morning. strange pattern, :eyes:
micah: spike as in numbers?
elena: can you paste a sample rejected payload? that helps debugging quick.
arjun: short log from router:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4x",
  "route": "reserved-high",
  "toolcall": {
    "name": "lookup_profile",
    "args": "{\"user_id\": 12345}"
  },
  "validation_error": "expected object for args but got string"
}
```
maya: aha — looks like adapter coerced args into a string during routing handoff when quota-route rewriting happened. seen similar in the proxy change last month.
arjun: that's what I suspected. the odd part: only requests routed to the "reserved-high" pool are affected, not the general pool.
ashley: can we confirm whether the router does any JSON stringify/merge when applying burst quotas? tx-ops config was touched at 07:12.
micah: checking tx-ops commit log... @ops-sig committed "quota-routing: attach burst token metadata" at 07:11:22. commit diff shows small change in route metadata merging code.
elena: low-risk reproduction: call model with fn_call where args is an object and force route to reserved-high. I can run a curl test in a sec.
arjun: repro would be great. meanwhile metrics-bot: publish the validation-rejects-by-route graph to the channel?
metrics-bot: posted -> https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/validators/rejects-by-route?ts=3498765432 :bar_chart:
maya: looking at the dashboard, rejects for reserved-high jumped from ~12/hr to ~420/hr at 07:12. general pool flat.
ashley: could be a serialization step in the route decorator. In code we do: `route_meta = {**route_meta, **req_metadata}` — if req_metadata.args is an object, some internal representation might stringify it when shallow-copied into a string-keyed metadata bag.
micah: sounds plausible. but why would only reserved-high be affected? different route adapter maybe. reserved-high uses the "quota-refactor" adapter.
elena: I ran the curl test against canary: when forced to quota-refactor route, the request body that reaches the validator shows `toolcall.args` as a JSON string. when routed to general it remains an object. attaching logs: `payload.args_type=string` vs `args_type=object`.
arjun: ok next action: rollback the metadata merge in quota-refactor adapter or coerce back before validation. what's the impact if we coerce? any risk of double-stringifying?
maya: coercion before validation is safer for quick mitigation. add a step: if toolcall.args is type string and looks like JSON, attempt JSON.parse and set it. that will unbreak most cases. long-term we should fix adapter merge.
ashley: agree. create a canary patch on reserved-high pool to run unstringify step. release as a hotfix with a short window canary.
micah: I'll open a short-lived canary rollout: tag `quota-refactor-fix-2026-03-20`. deploy-bot: can you run canary?
deploy-bot: starting canary deploy of quota-refactor-fix-2026-03-20 to reserved-high (5% traffic) 
metrics-bot: scheduled sampling for validation failures to be retained at full fidelity for 10m during canary window.
arjun: also add telemetry flag so we can distinguish coerced-then-fixed events: `metadata.fix_attempt=unstringify-v1`. need that in logs so we can back out if noisy.
elena: done — added try/except and only set when parse succeeds. also emit telemetry `unstringify_succeeded` or `unstringify_failed`.
micah: canary live at 07:35. so far validation rejects down 95% on reserved-high.
arjun: nice. leave canary at 5% for 30m and then promote.
maya: followup for postmortem: add a lint or test that catches metadata merging behaviors that convert nested objects to strings when route metadata merges occur.
ashley: I'll create a short RFC for router metadata contract and add an e2e test that simulates quota-augmentation flow.
micah: rolling to 50% now. no anomalies in latency or error budgets.
metrics-bot: validation rejects for reserved-high dropped to baseline.
arjun: thanks everyone. please add the incident note to postmortems/ with the timeline + dashboard links. I'll draft it and ping for review. :thumbsup:
metrics-bot: incident note created -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-20-qa-route-unstringify
ops-sig: marking followups: router-contract-rfc, validator-breakdown-dashboard, e2e-test for metadata-merge.
ashley: tagging owners on followups: @elena for e2e test, @maya for dashboard changes, @arjun for incident draft.
arjun: will do. closing thread once postmortem up.
